decisive_items: annular, arciform, and polycyclic morphology, central clearing, and purpuric edges
recurrent 3‐day outbreaks, always at the same locations, and resolved spontaneously without residual injury
Lesions were symmetrically distributed on the anterior thighs in a mirror‐image pattern
response.rationale: The morphology and recurrent self-limited course without residual injury fit an annular erythema best; the extensive negative workup supports a benign cutaneous diagnosis, whereas EM, vasculitis, and urticaria have important atypical features.

rejected.why: True target lesions are not described and the fixed 3-day pruritic recurrences without a trigger are atypical for erythema multiforme.
Normal complement and inflammatory markers, absence of systemic symptoms, and resolution without residual injury argue against vasculitis despite purpuric edges.
Symmetric mirror-image fixed recurrences, purpuric edges, and 3-day episode duration are atypical for ordinary urticaria despite pruritus and self-resolution.
